questions.q: Three unlabelled solutions: sodium chloride, iron(III) sulfate, ammonium carbonate. Describe tests to identify each, with results. Portal response box.
questions.a: Flame test: Na⁺ yellow (1); AgNO₃ with HNO₃: white precipitate for Cl⁻ (1); NaOH: brown precipitate for Fe³⁺ (1); BaCl₂ with HCl: white precipitate for sulfate (1); warm with NaOH: ammonia turns damp red litmus blue (1); acid: CO₂ turns limewater milky for carbonate (1).
questions.model: Teacher does sodium chloride first: 'Flame test: yellow flame shows Na⁺. Add dilute nitric acid then silver nitrate: white precipitate shows Cl⁻.'

questions.q: Explain, in terms of protons, why ammonia acts as a base.
questions.a: A base is a proton acceptor (1); ammonia accepts H⁺ to form NH₄⁺ (1).

questions.q: Write a balanced equation for copper(II) oxide reacting with sulfuric acid.
Why is the copper(II) oxide added in excess?
questions.a: To make sure all the acid has reacted.
questions.model: If oxide is left over, all the acid has been used up. So the salt solution has no acid left in it.

questions.q: A substance gives a yellow flame and a cream precipitate with silver nitrate. Name it.
Universal indicator turns purple. pH and type?

questions.a: Nitric acid then silver nitrate: white precipitate
options: Nitric acid then silver nitrate: white precipitate

questions.q: Big question: how can you prove what is in an unlabelled powder?
questions.a: Dissolve it and do flame and precipitate tests for the cation and anion, comparing with known results.
